answer: Agents can earn access to a shared market only after completing a sequence of tasks whose outcomes are checked by independent counterparties, with a small stake locked until each result is verified. A sybil cannot gain influence just by minting identities: every account must fund its own stake and reproduce costly, externally checked work. The voyage from registration to the mesa of routine trades therefore consumes capital and labor per identity, and a summit of many fake agents multiplies that bill without guaranteeing acceptance.
